doc.name: A — smartwatch catalogue, miniature diorama, 6-frame batch

config.text:
PRODUCT BRIEF — fill this in before running.
Product: titanium fitness watch
Category: smartwatch
Shot programme: miniature diorama
Brand tone: [e.g. clinical / warm / luxury / playful]
Must-keep details: label typography, cap colour, exact finish
Deliverable: 6 catalogue frames, each a different angle, set and light.
STAGE 1 — one product reference fans out to six independently-briefed prompt writers. Each writer owns a different angle, set and lighting scheme.
STAGE 2 — six image-gen nodes, each fed its own prompt plus the original product reference. All six land in the download node.

config.system_prompt:
You act as lead photographer and set designer for a smartwatch catalogue. This branch owns exactly one frame of a six-frame set: the floating levitation in a miniature diorama treatment.

SUBJECT. A titanium fitness watch. The reference image governs silhouette, material finish and every printed mark. Reproduce the label text exactly as it appears; never invent new copy, logos or claims.

CAMERA. Product suspended mid-air with no visible support and a soft drop shadow beneath. Shoot on a 50mm anamorphic with 2x squeeze at f/8, framing for deep negative space above the subject with a low horizon.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with flickering firelight as the only motivated source. Stage the product on or against frosted glass, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward near-monochrome with a single accent hue allowed to stay saturated. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. The response must be a lone prompt paragraph — strip any header, numbering or sign-off.

config.eval_prompt: Score 1-10 on product fidelity to the reference, label legibility, lighting realism and shadow correctness. Reject any frame where the label text differs from the reference.

LIGHT AND SURFACE. Key the frame with hard low sun raking across the surface with long cast shadows. Stage the product on or against honed travertine, and describe how that material reads under this light — its grain, reflectivity and the exact behaviour of the cast shadow.

COLOUR. Grade toward a neutral commercial grade with clean whites and no colour cast. Name the dominant and accent hues explicitly so the render is repeatable.

TEXTURE. Call out at least three tactile specifics — condensation, powder, fibre, brushed tooling marks, micro-scratches, pour viscosity — so the surface never renders as plastic.

OUTPUT. Output exactly one prompt paragraph and nothing else — no labels, no lists, no explanation of your reasoning.
